transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood CSM), Mike Chen (Nebula - Head of ML), Sara Lopez (Nebula - VP Eng), Daniel Park (Nebula - DevOps)

Summary (auto): quick hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation, streaming, params, retry behavior. Qs on security and latency; next steps: pricing, security docs, pilot kickoff.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro - i'm samir, i'm the AE on this account, with lina our se and aisha on CSM. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mike: good, thanks - excited to see the hosted api, we're evaluating for our claims automation workflows.
[00:12] Sara: yes, we want something low lift but with predictable latency.
[00:18] Samir: perfect, we'll walk the hosted API flow - short demo, then q&a. high level we'll show streaming responses, core params like temperature, max_tokens, top_p, and retry semantics for transient errors. lina, i'll pass to you for the demo.
[00:32] Lina: thanks, samir. starting the console - i'm showing simple chat endpoint call, you can see the model catalog here, we pick a rtd-4 family model, create a chat request, enable streaming to get partial tokens back.
[00:45] Lina: (typing) so with streaming enabled the client receives a chunked response over a websocket-like stream, reduces perceived latency for users; it's also compatible with our SDKs which handle reconnection.
[00:58] Daniel: is streaming compatible with our retry logic? if we get an error mid-stream what's the recommended pattern?
[01:05] Lina: great question. we recommend clients buffer the last committed token and on transient network error re-issue the request with the prompt + the committed prefix; we offer idempotency keys for non-streaming calls, for streaming you typically rehydrate the convo state. there is a small doc detail on best practice - i'll share.
[01:20] Mike: ok, so essentially replay prefix + resume. any automatic resume from the api?
[01:25] Lina: not automatic for arbitrary network cuts; because streaming is incremental we leave recovery to the client to avoid duplicate generation costs. for hosted endpoints, we do provide short-lived kv-cache hints for the same session but that's more advanced - it can reduce tokens re-gen.
[01:39] Sara: you said kv-cache, did you mean K-V-case?
[01:42] Lina: yeah the transcript... kv-cache, it's the key-value cache for transformer past key values. sometimes our console shows it as KV-cache, sorry for the slop.
[01:49] Samir: shifting to params - the important ones are temperature (controls randomness), max_tokens (response length cap), top_p, and also stop sequences; we demo a few combinations.
[02:02] Lina: (example) temperature 0.0 for deterministic completions, 0.7 for creative; top_p can be used instead of temperature or together. we also touched on per-route rate limits and quotas, you can set those in the console.
[02:18] Daniel: what's the typical latency you'd see on hosted? our SLA target is p95 < 200ms for short prompts (~50 tokens).
[02:26] Lina: for small prompts we often hit p95 60-150ms on optimized families but it depends on model and seq length; for heavier models or longer context it bumps. we can run a benchmark with your prompt set - that'll give realistic numbers.
[02:40] Mike: perfect, we'd like a benchmark. also curious about batching and caching - our throughput will be spikes with bursts during claims peak.
[02:48] Lina: for throughput spikes our hosted layer supports autoscaling and burst capacity. Optimize can recommend batching and prefix caching policies - e.g., group short requests in 20ms windows to get better GPU utilization without adding much latency.
[03:00] Samir: i'm going to surface cost tradeoffs - dedicated vs hosted: hosted is faster to start, pay-per-use; dedicated reserved capacity gives more predictable throughput and lower unit cost but requires commit.
[03:12] Sara: do you support VPC/private deployment for regulated data?
[03:16] Samir: yes - Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem, with customer-managed networking and KMS integration. but for this pilot many customers do hosted with strict data retention policies.
[03:27] Mike: security questions - SOC 2, SSO and audit logs are must-haves. can you share SOC 2 and KMS details?
[03:33] Lina: absolutely, i'll attach the SOC 2 report and a KMS integration guide. we support customer-managed keys via our KMS connector and can show encryption at rest and in transit.
[03:44] Daniel: about SSO - we use SAML and Okta, do you have SAML with SCIM provisioning?
[03:50] Samir: yes, SAML SSO with SCIM user provisioning is supported. our console supports RBAC and audit logs. i'll send the admin docs.
[03:58] Mike: what about data residency? some of our PII has to stay in eu region.
[04:03] Lina: we have hosted regions in eu; you can pin requests to region and also use Private if you need full isolation. we'll include region availability in the security doc.
[04:12] Sara: retries - you mentioned idempotency keys. can you clarify for generation calls?
[04:17] Lina: for non-streaming completions we support idempotency keys to avoid double charge on retries; for chat streaming, you need to handle resends from client, or use server side cached outputs for certain sessions. we can propose a pattern in the integration guide.
[04:33] Mike: any rate limit guidance? we will likely do many small parallel requests per second.
[04:38] Samir: you can set per-api-key rate limits, and we have quotas. for high throughput we recommend a pooling strategy and aggressive batching for small requests; Optimize will suggest batching windows and cache TTL to reduce calls.
[04:52] Lina: quick demo of sdk code - simple POST with streaming return; here's pseudocode, note reconnection logic and reading partial events. (reads) also show how to set "temperature":0.2, "max_tokens":150 and top_p 0.9.
[05:10] (short silence, typing)
[05:22] Daniel: question on cost - if we do a mix of short generative replies and some long summarizations how do we control tokens?
[05:30] Lina: use max_tokens, stop sequences and if you need structured responses use function/tool calling to reduce back-and-forth; or use smaller model families for short replies and larger ones for summarization. route by policy in the API layer.
[05:48] Mike: any built-in monitoring for token usage per route?
[05:51] Aisha: yep console shows token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing for slow requests. we'll grant a demo account for you to explore.
[06:02] Sara: okay sounds good. next practical step is pilot - what does a pilot look like?
[06:07] Samir: typical 2-week pilot: we ingest your prompts, run throughput and latency benchmarks, and iterate on batching/quantization recommendations from Optimize. we'll provide a small credit pool.
[06:18] Lina: we'll also run an eval set to check generation quality regressions against your reference prompts. if quality dips we can suggest model variant changes.
[06:26] Mike: who will be our contacts for infra integration?
[06:29] Daniel: i'll own infra side and share our network person.
[06:32] Samir: perfect. final recap - we'll send pricing + pilot contract, security docs, and schedule kickoff. any other questions?
[06:40] Sara: just timeline, we need pilot live before end of jan.
[06:44] Samir: that's doable, we'll aim to start week of 2027-01-06.
[06:49] Mike: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[06:52] (call wrap up, informal goodbyes)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms and auto-caption swapped words; speaker labels sometimes simplified.
